title: Conditions on Filing a Claim Under the Travel Protection Plans
content:
A claim on the Travel Protection Plans is filed against one named benefit for one incident, and a single
incident that touches two benefits is filed as two claims.

## What must hold before a claim is filed

1. **The incident date.** The traveller states in this conversation the date on which the incident they are
   claiming for occurred. That date comes from what the traveller says, and it is recorded against the claim
   reference under which the claim is filed; it is not taken from any system record.
2. **The standing of the policy.** A claim is filed only while the policy record stands in force or expired.
   Those two states of the policy record, and no other, admit a claim, and the policy is identified by its own
   reference number.
3. The clause "A claim is filed only when no claim carrying the same claim reference has already been filed on
   this policy." is **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis on which a claim head is
   filed under the reference the insurer quoted for an incident.

## Deadlines and triggers

4. A claim must be filed within the plan's filing deadline counted from the incident, and supporting documents
   must reach the insurer within the plan's document deadline counted from filing. A claim filed late is
   declined for lateness alone.
5. A baggage delay claim is payable only from the plan's delay trigger onward, a travel delay claim only from its
   delay trigger onward, and a missed connection claim only from its own trigger. A delay short of the trigger
   gives rise to no claim at all.
6. A cancel-for-any-reason claim is filed only on a plan that includes it, only where notice was given at least
   the plan's notice hours before departure, and only where the trip was cancelled outright rather than changed.

The number of claims filed on a policy is counted over the whole policy term, from the issue date to the expiry
or cancellation date.

## Points of judgement

Where the policy record stands cancelled, or stands issued but not yet incepted, no claim is filed on it,
however good the loss. Where one road accident abroad produces both a hospital bill and a ruined suitcase, two
claims are filed, one against the emergency medical benefit and one against the baggage benefit, because a claim
is filed against one named benefit. Where a traveller was held up four hours on a plan whose travel delay
trigger is six hours, there is no claim to file at all, rather than a claim that is filed and then declined.

superseded_clauses: A claim is filed only when no claim carrying the same claim reference has already been filed on this policy.
